instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F with a rack in the middle. Line a baking sheet with heavy-duty foil.
Trim a thin slice off the stem end of each squash so it stands up, then cut it in half lengthwise. Scoop out the seeds.
Set the halves cut side up on the baking sheet. Rub with the olive oil and sprinkle with 1 tsp of the salt and 1/2 tsp of the pepper. Flip them cut side down.
Roast for 40 to 50 minutes, until the bottoms are golden and a fork slides in easily.
Flip the halves cut side up and leave them until you can handle them, about 10 minutes. Turn the oven up to 425°F.
Scrape the squash into strands with a fork and transfer them to a large bowl.
Add the marinara, the remaining 3/4 tsp salt, the remaining 1/4 tsp pepper and 2 tsp chopped thyme. Toss. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Spread it in an ungreased 9 x 13 inch baking dish. Top with the mozzarella, then the Parmesan.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until the top is golden and the edges bubble.
Let it cool for a few minutes and sprinkle with a little more thyme.
method_notes: Once Upon a Chef is the lead (roast the squash cut side down, scrape, toss with marinara and thyme, top with mozzarella and Parmesan, bake at 425°F). Food Network's simpler version, which has no ratings, agrees on the shape of the dish. Adapted: the lead's butter and panko topping is left out to keep the dish gluten-free, and the marinara is listed as gluten-free, so check the label. Roasting whole squash is slow, so the dish honestly takes about 80 minutes.
